question: Several companies are building chips specialized for the transformer architecture. On such a chip, a medium-sized model generates at a rate on the order of:

options.feedback: That is roughly two orders of magnitude above a hosted frontier model. It is what makes a long stretch of generation cheap in wall-clock time, which changes what is worth building on top of a medium-sized model.

This would only be a few times faster than a hosted frontier model, which would not change much. The whole reason these chips are interesting is that they clear the hosted rate by a much wider margin than that.

That is the range a hosted frontier model already occupies, so a chip that delivered it would offer nothing new. The specialized chips buy speed at the price of model size, and the speed gain is dramatic.
That is what you get on a laptop with no GPU (graphics processing unit) -- the slow end of the range, not the fast end. Purpose-built inference hardware sits at the opposite extreme.
